title: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 01
titleEn: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 01

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following naturally occurring $\alpha$-amino acids is **achiral**?
questions.explanationEn: **Glycine** ($\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$) has two identical hydrogen atoms attached to the $\alpha$-carbon, so it lacks a chiral center and is achiral. All other 19 standard proteinogenic amino acids are chiral. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In Zeise's salt, $\text{K}[\text{PtCl}_3(\eta^2\text{-C}_2\text{H}_4)]\cdot\text{H}_2\text{O}$, coordination of ethylene to $\text{Pt(II)}$ causes the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bond length (compared to free $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) to
optionsEn: increase, and the ethylene $\text{C}=\text{C}$ axis lies perpendicular to the $\text{PtCl}_3$ plane
decrease, and the ethylene $\text{C}=\text{C}$ axis lies in the $\text{PtCl}_3$ plane
remain unchanged, and the complex is tetrahedral
increase, and the complex is an $18$-electron octahedral species
questions.explanationEn: By the Dewar–Chatt–Duncanson model, $\pi(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4) \to \text{Pt}(\sigma)$ donation and $\text{Pt}(d\pi) \to \pi^*(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4)$ back-donation both weaken and lengthen the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bond (from $133.7\text{ pm}$ to $137.5\text{ pm}$). Sterically and electronically, the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bond sits perpendicular to the square-planar $\text{PtCl}_3$ plane.

questions.questionTextEn: Treating chlorobenzene with $\text{NaNH}_2$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$ at $-33\,^\circ\text{C}$ converts it to aniline predominantly via which reactive intermediate?
questions.explanationEn: Because chlorobenzene lacks strongly electron-withdrawing *ortho*/*para* substituents, it cannot undergo $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$ via a Meisenheimer complex. Instead, strong amide base $\text{NH}_2^-$ induces 1,2-elimination of $\text{HCl}$ to generate **benzyne**, which subsequently adds $\text{NH}_3$ to yield aniline. Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A proton and an $\alpha$-particle (mass $\approx 4$ times the proton mass) possess the same kinetic energy. The ratio of the de Broglie wavelength of the proton to that of the $\alpha$-particle is
questions.explanationEn: Since $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$, at equal kinetic energy $K$, $\frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_\alpha} = \sqrt{\frac{m_\alpha}{m_p}} = \sqrt{4} = 2$, giving a ratio of $2 : 1$.

questions.questionTextEn: In aqueous solution at $298\text{ K}$, the anomalously high limiting molar ionic conductivity of $\text{H}^+$ ($349.6\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$) compared to $\text{Na}^+$ ($50.1\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$) is primarily due to
optionsEn: the absence of any hydration shell around $\text{H}^+$ in water.
lower viscosity of acidic solutions compared to neutral salt solutions.
structural proton hopping across hydrogen-bonded water chains (Grotthuss mechanism).
the smaller molar mass of $\text{H}^+$ giving it a higher thermal velocity.
questions.explanationEn: Protons in water exist as hydrated complexes ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$, $\text{H}_9\text{O}_4^+$) and conduct charge primarily via rapid proton-transfer relays along hydrogen-bonded water networks (the Grotthuss mechanism), rather than hydrodynamic Stokes diffusion.

questions.questionTextEn: For any gas obeying the van der Waals equation of state, the critical compressibility factor $Z_c = \dfrac{P_c V_{m,c}}{RT_c}$ is equal to
questions.explanationEn: Substituting the van der Waals critical constants $P_c = \frac{a}{27b^2}$, $V_{m,c} = 3b$, and $T_c = \frac{8a}{27Rb}$ gives $Z_c = \frac{(a/27b^2)(3b)}{R(8a/27Rb)} = \frac{3}{8} = 0.375$.

questions.questionTextEn: The hybridization of the central iodine atom and the molecular shape of $[\text{ICl}_4]^-$, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: Iodine has $7$ valence electrons; adding $1$ electron for the $-1$ charge gives $8$ electrons. Forming $4$ $\text{I}-\text{Cl}$ bonds leaves $4$ non-bonding electrons ($2$ lone pairs). Steric number $= 4 + 2 = 6$ ($sp^3d^2$). Placing the two lone pairs trans to each other minimizes lone pair–lone pair repulsion, giving a square planar shape ($D_{4h}$).

questions.questionTextEn: The IUPAC stereochemical descriptor for the alkene $\text{Br(Cl)C}=\text{C(CH}_2\text{OH)(CHO)}$ in which $-\text{Br}$ and $-\text{CHO}$ are on the **same side** of the double bond is
questions.explanationEn: By Cahn–Ingold–Prelog (CIP) rules: on C1, $-\text{Br}$ ($Z = 35$) outranks $-\text{Cl}$ ($Z = 17$); on C2, $-\text{CHO}$ (carbon bonded to $(\text{O}, \text{O}, \text{H})$) outranks $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (carbon bonded to $(\text{O}, \text{H}, \text{H})$). Since both higher-priority groups are on the same side, the configuration is $(Z)$.

questions.questionTextEn: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled simultaneously. The probability that the sum of the numbers on the top faces is $9$ is
questions.explanationEn: There are $6 \times 6 = 36$ equally likely outcomes. The outcomes summing to $9$ are $(3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3)$ — a total of $4$ outcomes. Hence $P = \frac{4}{36} = \frac{1}{9}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the Hinsberg test, an unknown amine reacts with benzenesulfonyl chloride ($\text{PhSO}_2\text{Cl}$) in aqueous $\text{KOH}$ to form a precipitate that is **insoluble** in aqueous $\text{KOH}$ and also **insoluble** in dilute aqueous $\text{HCl}$. The unknown amine is a
questions.explanationEn: A secondary amine forms an $N,N$-disubstituted sulfonamide ($\text{PhSO}_2\text{NR}_2$) that lacks an acidic $\text{N–H}$ proton (hence insoluble in aq. $\text{KOH}$) and is non-basic (hence insoluble in dilute $\text{HCl}$).

questions.questionTextEn: Thermal Claisen rearrangement of allyl phenyl ether ($\text{Ph}-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$) labeled with $^{14}\text{C}$ exclusively at the terminal methylene carbon ($=^{14}\text{CH}_2$) yields
optionsEn: 2-(prop-2-en-1-yl)phenol with $^{14}\text{C}$ attached directly to the benzene ring (benzylic carbon)
4-(prop-2-en-1-yl)phenol with $^{14}\text{C}$ attached directly to the benzene ring
questions.explanationEn: The aromatic Claisen rearrangement is a concerted $[3,3]$-sigmatropic shift followed by rapid keto–enol tautomerization (rearomatization). In the $[3,3]$ shift, the terminal $=^{14}\text{CH}_2$ carbon forms the new $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond directly to the *ortho* ring carbon, inverting the allyl chain so that $^{14}\text{C}$ ends up at the **benzylic carbon** of 2-allylphenol. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In the potentiometric titration of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ with $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ in $1\text{ M}$ $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ ($\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{Ce}^{4+} \to \text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{Ce}^{3+}$), given formal potentials $E^{\circ\prime}(\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}) = +0.77\text{ V}$ and $E^{\circ\prime}(\text{Ce}^{4+}/\text{Ce}^{3+}) = +1.61\text{ V}$, the electrode potential at the equivalence point is
questions.explanationEn: For a symmetric 1:1 redox titration ($n_1 = n_2 = 1$), the equivalence-point potential is $E_{\text{eq}} = \frac{n_1 E_1^{\circ\prime} + n_2 E_2^{\circ\prime}}{n_1 + n_2} = \frac{0.77 + 1.61}{2} = +1.19\text{ V}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the powder X-ray diffraction pattern of a face-centered cubic (fcc) metal, the ratio of $\sin^2\theta$ values for the first three allowed reflections is
questions.explanationEn: By Bragg's law for a cubic crystal, $\sin^2\theta = \frac{\lambda^2}{4a^2}(h^2 + k^2 + l^2) \propto (h^2 + k^2 + l^2)$. For fcc, $h, k, l$ must be all odd or all even, so the first three allowed planes are $(111), (200), (220)$, giving $h^2 + k^2 + l^2 = 3, 4, 8$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the **Kiliani–Fischer chain-lengthening synthesis**, D-arabinose (an aldopentose) is treated sequentially with (i) $\text{HCN}$, (ii) $\text{H}_2/\text{Pd-BaSO}_4$ (or hydrolysis to lactone followed by $\text{Na-Hg}$, $\text{pH } 3\text{--}5$). The two aldohexose products formed are
questions.explanationEn: Kiliani–Fischer synthesis adds one new stereogenic carbon at C2 while retaining the configurations of all original chiral centers (C2, C3, C4 of D-arabinose become C3, C4, C5 of the aldohexoses: $\text{OH}$ left, right, right). This yields the pair of **C2-epimers**: **D-glucose** and **D-mannose**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The molecular shapes of the polyiodide anions $\text{I}_3^-$ and $\text{I}_5^-$ (in solid salts such as $\text{Me}_4\text{N}^+\text{I}_5^-$), respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: $\text{I}_3^-$ has $2$ bond pairs and $3$ equatorial lone pairs ($\text{SN}=5$), giving a **linear** shape ($3\text{c}\text{--}4\text{e}$ bonding). $\text{I}_5^-$ is best viewed as a central $\text{I}^-$ donor coordinated to two $\text{I}_2$ molecules at roughly $95^\circ$, giving a **V-shaped (bent)** planar structure.

questions.questionTextEn: The exact analytical expression for the packing fraction of identical hard spheres in a body-centered cubic (bcc) lattice is
questions.explanationEn: In a bcc unit cell, $Z = 2$ and spheres touch along the body diagonal: $4r = \sqrt{3}\,a \implies a = \frac{4r}{\sqrt{3}}$. Thus $\text{Packing fraction} = \frac{2 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3}{(4r/\sqrt{3})^3} = \frac{\frac{8}{3}\pi}{64/(3\sqrt{3})} = \frac{\pi\sqrt{3}}{8} \approx 0.680$.

questions.questionTextEn: Ignoring electron spin, the total degeneracy of the $n = 4$ energy level of the hydrogen atom is
questions.explanationEn: In the hydrogen atom, energy depends only on the principal quantum number $n$. For $n = 4$, the allowed subshells are $4s (1), 4p (3), 4d (5), 4f (7)$, giving a spatial degeneracy of $1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = n^2 = 16$.

questions.questionTextEn: For $a > 0$, the value of the definite Gaussian integral $\displaystyle\int_0^{\infty} x^2 e^{-ax^2}\,dx$ is
questions.explanationEn: Using the standard Gaussian integral $\int_0^\infty e^{-ax^2}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{a}}$ and differentiating with respect to $a$: $-\int_0^\infty x^2 e^{-ax^2}\,dx = -\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{\pi}\,a^{-3/2}$, giving $\int_0^\infty x^2 e^{-ax^2}\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{a^3}}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the Reformatsky reaction of benzaldehyde with ethyl 2-bromopropanoate and activated $\text{Zn}$ dust in dry $\text{THF}$ followed by aqueous $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ workup, the major product is
questions.explanationEn: Activated $\text{Zn}$ inserts into the $\text{C}-\text{Br}$ bond of ethyl 2-bromopropanoate to form the zinc enolate $\text{BrZn}-\text{CH(Me)CO}_2\text{Et}$, which undergoes nucleophilic addition to benzaldehyde (without self-condensing with the ester) to afford the $\beta$-hydroxy ester **ethyl 3-hydroxy-2-methyl-3-phenylpropanoate**. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The lowest-energy spin-allowed $d\text{--}d$ absorption band ($\nu_1$) in the electronic spectrum of octahedral $[\text{Cr(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ ($d^3$) corresponds to the transition
questions.explanationEn:
For a $d^3$ octahedral complex ($t_{2g}^3$, ground term $^4A_{2g}$), the three spin-allowed transitions are $
u_1$: $^4A_{2g} 	o {}^4T_{2g}$, $
u_2$: $^4A_{2g} 	o {}^4T_{1g}(F)$, and $
u_3$: $^4A_{2g} 	o {}^4T_{1g}(P)$. Because $^4T_{2g}$ does not mix with any other quartet state, its energy above $^4A_{2g}$ is strictly equal to $\Delta_o$.

questions.questionTextEn: Given the standard reduction potentials in acidic medium: $E^\circ(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}^+) = +0.15\text{ V}$ and $E^\circ(\text{Cu}^+/\text{Cu}) = +0.52\text{ V}$, the standard EMF $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$ for the disproportionation $2\text{Cu}^+(\text{aq}) \to \text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + \text{Cu}(s)$ and its spontaneity are
questions.explanationEn: Disproportionation combines reduction $\text{Cu}^+ + e^- \to \text{Cu}$ ($E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} = +0.52\text{ V}$) with oxidation $\text{Cu}^+ \to \text{Cu}^{2+} + e^-$ ($E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = +0.15\text{ V}$). Thus $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 0.52 - 0.15 = +0.37\text{ V} > 0$, making the disproportionation thermodynamically spontaneous.

questions.questionTextEn: Which glycosidic linkage connects the two monosaccharide units in **lactose** (milk sugar)?
questions.explanationEn: **Lactose** is $4\text{-}O\text{-}(\beta\text{-D-galactopyranosyl})-\text{D-glucopyranose}$, featuring a **$\beta\text{-(1}\to\text{4)}$ glycosidic bond** from D-galactose (C1) to D-glucose (C4). (Maltose is $\alpha\text{-(1}\to\text{4)}$ Glc–Glc; cellobiose is $\beta\text{-(1}\to\text{4)}$ Glc–Glc; sucrose is $\alpha\text{-(1}\to\text{2)}$-$\beta$ Glc–Fru.) Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following functions is an eigenfunction of the operator $\hat{A} = \dfrac{d^2}{dx^2} - 2\dfrac{d}{dx}$, and what is its corresponding eigenvalue?
questions.explanationEn: Applying $\hat{A} = \frac{d^2}{dx^2} - 2\frac{d}{dx}$ to $f(x) = e^{3x}$ yields $\hat{A}e^{3x} = 9e^{3x} - 2(3e^{3x}) = 3e^{3x}$, confirming $e^{3x}$ is an eigenfunction with eigenvalue $3$. For $\sin(2x)$ and $\cos(3x)$, the first derivative mixes $\sin$ and $\cos$, so they are not eigenfunctions.

questions.questionTextEn: Following standard rules for significant figures, the result of the calculation $\dfrac{(12.45 - 12.10) \times 4.215}{2.00}$ should be reported as
questions.explanationEn:
Step 1 (subtraction): $12.45 - 12.10 = 0.35$ (retains $2$ decimal places $\implies 2$ significant figures).
Step 2 (multiplication/division): $\frac{0.35 \times 4.215}{2.00} = 0.737625$. Limited by $0.35$ ($2$ significant figures), the final result must be rounded to $2$ significant figures: $0.74$.

questions.questionTextEn: According to Bent's rule, in the trigonal bipyramidal molecule $\text{PCl}_3\text{F}_2$, the positions occupied by the two fluorine atoms and the net dipole moment ($\mu$) of the molecule are
optionsEn: one axial and one equatorial, and $\mu > 0$
questions.explanationEn: In a trigonal bipyramid ($sp^3d$), equatorial orbitals have higher $s$-character ($sp^2$, $33.3\%\,s$) and axial orbitals have higher $p$/$d$-character ($pd$, $0\%\,s$). By Bent's rule, more electronegative substituents prefer orbitals with less $s$-character, so both $\text{F}$ atoms occupy the two axial sites and all three $\text{Cl}$ atoms occupy the equatorial sites ($D_{3h}$ symmetry), giving $\mu = 0$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the base-catalyzed dehydration of 4-hydroxybutan-2-one ($\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$) to but-3-en-2-one with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, the mechanism is best classified as
questions.explanationEn: 4-Hydroxybutan-2-one has a poor leaving group ($-\text{OH}$) and an acidic $\alpha$-hydrogen adjacent to the ketone carbonyl. Base rapidly deprotonates the $\alpha$-carbon to form a resonance-stabilized enolate carbanion, which then expels $\text{OH}^-$ in the rate-determining step — a textbook **$\text{E1cb}$** elimination. Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In the most stable chair conformation of *trans*-1-*tert*-butyl-3-methylcyclohexane, the orientations of the $-^t\text{Bu}$ group (C1) and the $-\text{CH}_3$ group (C3) are
questions.explanationEn: In any 1,3-*trans*-disubstituted cyclohexane, one substituent must be equatorial and the other axial. Because the $A$-value of $-^t\text{Bu}$ ($\sim 20.5\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) vastly exceeds that of $-\text{CH}_3$ ($\sim 7.3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), the ring locks with $-^t\text{Bu}$ equatorial and $-\text{CH}_3$ axial.

questions.questionTextEn:
For the reaction $2\text{NO}(\text{g}) + 2\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \to \text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{g})$, initial rate measurements at $1100\text{ K}$ yield:
- Run 1: $[\text{NO}] = 0.10\text{ M}$, $[\text{H}_2] = 0.10\text{ M}$, $r_0 = 1.2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M s}^{-1}$
- Run 2: $[\text{NO}] = 0.20\text{ M}$, $[\text{H}_2] = 0.10\text{ M}$, $r_0 = 4.8 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M s}^{-1}$
- Run 3: $[\text{NO}] = 0.20\text{ M}$, $[\text{H}_2] = 0.30\text{ M}$, $r_0 = 1.44 \times 10^{-2}\text{ M s}^{-1}$
The rate law and rate constant $k$ are
questions.explanationEn: Comparing Run 2 and Run 1: doubling $[\text{NO}]$ at fixed $[\text{H}_2]$ quadruples $r_0$ ($4.8/1.2 = 4 = 2^2$), so order in $\text{NO}$ is $2$. Comparing Run 3 and Run 2: tripling $[\text{H}_2]$ at fixed $[\text{NO}]$ triples $r_0$ ($14.4/4.8 = 3 = 3^1$), so order in $\text{H}_2$ is $1$. From Run 1: $k = \frac{1.2 \times 10^{-3}}{(0.10)^2(0.10)} = \frac{1.2 \times 10^{-3}}{10^{-3}} = 1.2\text{ M}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In 2,3,4-trihydroxypentanedioic acid ($\text{HO}_2\text{C–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CO}_2\text{H}$), the central carbon (C3) is a **pseudoasymmetric** ($r/s$) stereocenter in
optionsEn: the two optically inactive *meso* stereoisomers, $(2R,3r,4S)$ and $(2R,3s,4S)$
the optically active $(2R,4R)$ and $(2S,4S)$ enantiomeric pair
questions.explanationEn: A pseudoasymmetric carbon is bonded to two constitutionally identical but enantiomorphic ligands (one $R$ and one $S$) plus two different achiral groups ($-\text{H}$ and $-\text{OH}$). In $(2R,4S)$ isomers, C2 is $R$ and C4 is $S$, making C3 pseudoasymmetric and generating two distinct achiral *meso* diastereomers: $(2R,3r,4S)$ and $(2R,3s,4S)$. In $(2R,4R)$ and $(2S,4S)$, C2 and C4 have the same configuration so C3 is not stereogenic.

questions.questionTextEn: The aqueous solubility of alkaline earth metal sulfates decreases down Group 2 ($\text{BeSO}_4 > \text{MgSO}_4 > \text{CaSO}_4 > \text{SrSO}_4 > \text{BaSO}_4$), whereas that of their hydroxides increases down the group ($\text{Be(OH)}_2 < \text{Mg(OH)}_2 < \text{Ca(OH)}_2 < \text{Sr(OH)}_2 < \text{Ba(OH)}_2$). This opposite trend arises because
optionsEn: for large $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, the lattice enthalpy changes little down the group while hydration enthalpy drops sharply; for small $\text{OH}^-$, the lattice enthalpy drops faster than hydration enthalpy
for large $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, the hydration enthalpy increases down the group; for small $\text{OH}^-$, the hydration enthalpy decreases
alkaline earth hydroxides are purely covalent while sulfates are purely ionic
entropy of solution is positive for all sulfates and negative for all hydroxides
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{MSO}_4$, $r_-(\text{SO}_4^{2-}) \gg r_+$, so $r_+ + r_-$ and hence lattice energy $|U_0|$ change very little down the group, whereas $|\Delta H_{\text{hyd}}(\text{M}^{2+})|$ decreases rapidly, making dissolution less favorable down the group. In $\text{M(OH)}_2$, $r_-(\text{OH}^-)$ is small, so $|U_0|$ decreases more steeply than $|\Delta H_{\text{hyd}}|$ as $r_+$ increases, increasing solubility down the group.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding metal–carbonyl ($\text{M}-\text{CO}$) bonding is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: Metal carbonyl bonding is synergistic: $\text{CO} \to \text{M}$ $\sigma$-donation strengthens $\text{M} \to \text{CO}$ $\pi$-back-donation and vice versa.
Increasing $\pi$-back-donation into the $\pi^*(\text{CO})$ orbital shortens the $\text{M}-\text{C}$ bond and lengthens the $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond.
For neutral homoleptic metal carbonyls, $\nu_{\text{CO}}$ is lower than that of free $\text{CO}$ ($2143\text{ cm}^{-1}$).
In the cationic carbonyl $[\text{Mn(CO)}_6]^+$, $\text{M} \to \text{CO}$ $\pi$-back-bonding is stronger than in $[\text{Cr(CO)}_6]$.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A), (B), (C) are all true.
- (D) False: Positive charge on $[\text{Mn(CO)}_6]^+$ contracts the $3d$ orbitals and reduces back-bonding relative to neutral $[\text{Cr(CO)}_6]$.

questions.questionTextEn: For any two non-zero three-dimensional vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \vec{0}$ if and only if $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are perpendicular.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** Cross product is anticommutative.
- **(B) True:** $\vec{A} \times \vec{B}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{A}$, so their dot product is zero.
- **(C) True:** Lagrange's identity: $(AB\sin\theta)^2 + (AB\cos\theta)^2 = A^2 B^2$.
- **(D) False:** $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \vec{0}$ iff they are parallel/antiparallel ($\sin\theta = 0$), not perpendicular.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about interhalogen compounds and polyhalide ions is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: $[\text{ICl}_2]^-$ is linear with iodine at the center and three equatorial lone pairs.
Interhalogens like $\text{ICl}$ are generally less reactive than $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{Cl}_2$.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: $\text{IF}_7$ has $7$ bond pairs and $0$ lone pairs ($sp^3d^3$, pentagonal bipyramidal).
- (B) True: $\text{IF}_5$ has $5$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair ($sp^3d^2$, square pyramidal).
- (C) True: $[\text{ICl}_2]^-$ has $2$ bond pairs and $3$ equatorial lone pairs ($sp^3d$, linear).
- (D) False: Heteronuclear $X-X'$ bonds are generally weaker and more polar than homonuclear $X-X$ bonds (except $\text{F}_2$), making interhalogens *more* reactive than the parent halogens (except $\text{F}_2$).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements comparing organolithium ($\text{RLi}$), Grignard ($\text{RMgX}$), and Gilman cuprate ($\text{R}_2\text{CuLi}$) reagents is/are correct?
optionsEn: $\text{RLi}$ is more nucleophilic and basic than $\text{RMgX}$ because the $\text{C}-\text{Li}$ bond has greater ionic character than the $\text{C}-\text{Mg}$ bond.
$\text{R}_2\text{CuLi}$ undergoes predominantly 1,4-conjugate addition with $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketones, whereas $\text{RLi}$ favors 1,2-addition.
$\text{R}_2\text{CuLi}$ couples efficiently with primary alkyl bromides and vinyl iodides (Corey–House synthesis).
$\text{RMgX}$ reacts selectively with carboxylic acids to give ketones in high yield.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** $\text{Li}$ ($\chi = 0.98$) is more electropositive than $\text{Mg}$ ($\chi = 1.31$), making $\text{C}-\text{Li}$ more polar and reactive.
- **(B) Correct:** Soft cuprates favor 1,4-addition; hard organolithiums favor 1,2-addition.
- **(C) Correct:** Corey–House coupling uses $\text{R}_2\text{CuLi}$ with primary/vinyl/aryl halides.
- **(D) Incorrect:** $\text{RMgX}$ is simply protonated by $\text{R}'\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ to give $\text{R}-\text{H}$ and $\text{R}'\text{CO}_2\text{MgX}$ (whereas 2 equiv of $\text{RLi}$ can convert $\text{R}'\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ to a ketone).
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following is/are **electrode(s) of the second kind** (metal–insoluble salt–anion electrodes)?
questions.explanationEn: Electrodes of the second kind consist of a metal in contact with a sparingly soluble salt of that metal and a solution containing the common anion: calomel (A), $\text{Ag}/\text{AgCl}$ (B), and $\text{Hg}/\text{Hg}_2\text{SO}_4$ (C). SHE (D) is a gas-ion electrode.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following products can be obtained directly from benzenediazonium chloride ($\text{PhN}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$) in a single step using the specified reagent?
optionsEn: 4-Hydroxyazobenzene using phenol in mildly alkaline aqueous solution ($\text{pH } 9\text{--}10$)
questions.explanationEn:
All four are classic single-step transformations of $\text{PhN}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$:
- **(A)** Sandmeyer cyanation with $\text{CuCN/KCN}$ gives $\text{PhCN}$.
- **(B)** Direct nucleophilic/SET iodination with aq. $\text{KI}$ (no $\text{Cu}$ catalyst needed) gives $\text{PhI}$.
- **(C)** Reductive deamination with $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ gives $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$.
- **(D)** Electrophilic azo coupling with phenoxide at $\text{pH } 9\text{--}10$ gives 4-hydroxyazobenzene.
Hence, **(A), (B), (C), and (D)** are all correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The correct statement(s) regarding $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectroscopy is/are
optionsEn: Increasing the applied magnetic field $B_0$ increases the energy gap $\Delta E$ between the $\alpha$ and $\beta$ spin states.
Chemical shift $\delta$ (in ppm) is independent of the applied magnetic field strength $B_0$.
The spin–spin coupling constant $J$ (in Hz) is independent of the applied magnetic field strength $B_0$.
More shielded protons resonate at higher $\delta$ (downfield) values.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** $\Delta E = \hbar\gamma B_0 \propto B_0$.
- **(B) True:** $\delta$ is normalized by the operating frequency, making it field-independent.
- **(C) True:** $J$ (in Hz) is an intrinsic through-bond interaction independent of $B_0$.
- **(D) False:** More shielded protons experience a smaller local field and resonate at *lower* $\delta$ (upfield).

questions.questionTextEn: Among the following thermodynamic quantities, which is/are **state function(s)**?
questions.explanationEn: $H$, $A$, and $S$ are state functions whose changes depend only on initial and final states. Heat $q$ (even along a reversible path) is a path function, though $\delta q_{\text{rev}}/T = dS$ is an exact differential.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ and $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactions is/are true?
optionsEn: Polar aprotic solvents such as DMF and DMSO accelerate $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactions of anionic nucleophiles by leaving the anion poorly solvated.
In polar protic solvents, the nucleophilicity order of halide ions is $\text{I}^- > \text{Br}^- > \text{Cl}^- > \text{F}^-$.
An $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ solvolysis of an optically pure chiral secondary alkyl halide always gives a $100\%$ racemic mixture.
Neopentyl bromide ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCH}_2\text{Br}$) undergoes $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ substitution extremely slowly due to severe $\beta$-branching steric hindrance.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Polar aprotic solvents solvate cations well but do not hydrogen-bond to anions, increasing anion nucleophilicity.
- **(B) Correct:** In protic solvents, small hard $\text{F}^-$ is tightly caged by H-bonds, whereas large polarizable $\text{I}^-$ is weakly solvated and reacts fastest.
- **(C) Incorrect:** Because of intimate ion-pair shielding on the departing face, $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ solvolysis typically gives partial inversion (excess inversion over retention) rather than exact $100\%$ racemization.
- **(D) Correct:** Although primary, neopentyl bromide is sterically blocked at the backside by the bulky *tert*-butyl group.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (D)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following species is/are **aromatic** according to Hückel's rule?
questions.explanationEn: Tropylium cation ($6\pi$), $\text{C}_8\text{H}_8^{2-}$ ($10\pi$, planar), and squarate dianion ($2\pi$ aromatic ring stabilized by four $\text{C–O}^-$ oxygens) are all aromatic. Cyclobutadiene ($4\pi$) is antiaromatic.

questions.questionTextEn: According to the $18$-electron rule, the number of $\text{Mn}-\text{Mn}$ bonds in $\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Total valence electrons (TVE) $= 2(7) + 10(2) = 34\text{ e}^-$. Number of $\text{M}-\text{M}$ bonds $= \frac{18n - \text{TVE}}{2} = \frac{36 - 34}{2} = 1$.

questions.questionTextEn: A closed system absorbs $500\text{ J}$ of heat from its surroundings and performs $180\text{ J}$ of work on the surroundings. The change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) of the system is _______ $\text{J}$. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Using IUPAC sign convention ($q = +500\text{ J}$, $w = -180\text{ J}$): $\Delta U = q + w = 500 - 180 = 320\text{ J}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The value of the definite integral $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin x \cos^2 x\,dx$ is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: Substituting $u = \cos x$, $du = -\sin x\,dx$: $\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin x\cos^2 x\,dx = \int_0^1 u^2\,du = \left[\frac{u^3}{3}\right]_0^1 = \frac{1}{3} \approx 0.33$.

questions.questionTextEn: The number of stereogenic carbon centers in 1,2,3,4-tetrabromopentane is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{BrCH}_2\text{–CH(Br)–CH(Br)–CH(Br)–CH}_3$, C1 has two hydrogens and C5 has three hydrogens (neither is stereogenic), whereas C2, C3, and C4 each bear four distinct groups, giving $3$ stereogenic carbon centers.

questions.questionTextEn: For a particle in a one-dimensional box, the ratio of the energy of the $n = 4$ level to that of the $n = 2$ level ($E_4 / E_2$) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Since $E_n \propto n^2$, the ratio is $\frac{E_4}{E_2} = \frac{4^2}{2^2} = \frac{16}{4} = 4$.

questions.questionTextEn: The number of constitutionally distinct mononitronaphthalene isomers possible is _______.
questions.explanationEn: By $D_{2h}$ symmetry, naphthalene has only two chemically non-equivalent sets of ring hydrogens: the four $\alpha$-positions (C1, C4, C5, C8) and the four $\beta$-positions (C2, C3, C6, C7). Thus, **$2$** mononitronaphthalene isomers exist (1-nitronaphthalene and 2-nitronaphthalene).

questions.questionTextEn: The number of chemically non-equivalent sets of protons (signals) in the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of 1,3-dimethoxybenzene ($m$-dimethoxybenzene) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: 1,3-Dimethoxybenzene ($C_{2v}$ symmetry) has $4$ non-equivalent proton sets: (1) both $-\text{OCH}_3$ groups ($6\text{H}$), (2) H2 ($1\text{H}$), (3) H4 and H6 ($2\text{H}$), and (4) H5 ($1\text{H}$).

questions.questionTextEn: A $0.010\text{ M}$ aqueous solution of a weak monobasic acid has molar conductivity $\Lambda_m = 19.5\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$ and limiting molar conductivity $\Lambda_m^\circ = 390.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$ at $298\text{ K}$. Its degree of dissociation $\alpha$ is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: $\alpha = \frac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\circ} = \frac{19.5}{390.0} = 0.05$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Treatment of cyclopentanone with $m$-CPBA yields a cyclic ester (lactone) as the major product. The molecular weight of this lactone is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn: Baeyer–Villiger oxidation of cyclopentanone ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_8\text{O}$) inserts an oxygen atom into the ring to form $\delta$-valerolactone (tetrahydro-2$H$-pyran-2-one, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$). Its molecular weight is $5(12) + 8(1) + 2(16) = 100\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: According to Slater's rules, the effective nuclear charge ($Z_{\text{eff}}$) experienced by the $4s$ valence electron in a potassium atom ($Z = 19$) is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*

In a Diels–Alder reaction, $6.60\text{ g}$ of cyclopentadiene ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_6$) is reacted with $12.0\text{ g}$ of maleic anhydride ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_2\text{O}_3$) to afford $13.94\text{ g}$ of the $[4+2]$ cycloadduct ($\text{C}_9\text{H}_8\text{O}_3$). The percentage yield of the reaction is _______ $\%$. *(round off to the nearest integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn:
Molar masses: cyclopentadiene $= 66\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, maleic anhydride $= 98\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, adduct $= 164\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
- Moles of cyclopentadiene $= 6.60/66 = 0.100\text{ mol}$ (limiting reagent).
- Moles of maleic anhydride $= 12.0/98 = 0.122\text{ mol}$.
- Theoretical yield $= 0.100 \times 164 = 16.40\text{ g}$.
- Percentage yield $= (13.94 / 16.40) \times 100\% = \mathbf{85}\%$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Cyclohexanone is subjected to the following reaction sequence:
(i) $m$-CPBA in $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$; (ii) $\text{LiAlH}_4$ in $\text{THF}$, then $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$; (iii) excess PCC in $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$; (iv) aq. $\text{NaOH}$, $\Delta$.
The molecular weight of the final major organic product is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn:
Step (i): Baeyer–Villiger oxidation of cyclohexanone gives $\varepsilon$-caprolactone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$).
Step (ii): $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduction gives hexane-1,6-diol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}\text{O}_2$).
Step (iii): Excess PCC oxidizes both primary alcohols to hexanedial ($\text{OHC}(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{CHO}$, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$).
Step (iv): Intramolecular aldol condensation forms cyclopent-1-ene-1-carbaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_8\text{O}$).
Molecular weight $= 6(12) + 8(1) + 16 = \mathbf{96}\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($d^8$) in an oxide lattice with $\Delta_o = 108\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9}\Delta_o$, the octahedral site preference energy ($\text{OSPE} = |\text{CFSE}_{\text{oct}}| - |\text{CFSE}_{\text{tet}}|$) is _______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn:
For $d^8$ ($\text{Ni}^{2+}$):
- Octahedral ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^2$): $|\text{CFSE}_{\text{oct}}| = 1.2\Delta_o = 1.2 \times 108 = 129.6\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
- Tetrahedral ($e^4 t_2^4$): $|\text{CFSE}_{\text{tet}}| = 0.8\Delta_t = 0.8 \times \frac{4}{9}(108) = 0.8 \times 48 = 38.4\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
Hence, $\text{OSPE} = 129.6 - 38.4 = 91.2\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: At $298\text{ K}$, a $0.050\text{ M}$ aqueous solution of a weak monobasic acid has $\Lambda_m = 7.80\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Lambda_m^\circ = 390.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$. The $\text{p}K_a$ of the acid is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: $\alpha = \frac{7.80}{390.0} = 0.020$. By Ostwald's dilution law, $K_a = \frac{c\alpha^2}{1-\alpha} = \frac{0.050 \times (0.020)^2}{0.980} = 2.0408e-05$. Hence $\text{p}K_a = -\log_{10}(2.0408e-05) = 4.690 \approx 4.69$.

questions.questionTextEn:
From the following Born–Haber cycle data for $\text{CaO}(s)$, calculate the second electron gain enthalpy ($\text{O}^-(g) + e^- \to \text{O}^{2-}(g)$) of oxygen in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$: _______ *(answer in integer)*

[Given: $\Delta_f H^\circ(\text{CaO}) = -635\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$; $\Delta_{\text{sub}} H^\circ(\text{Ca}) = +178\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$; $\text{IE}_1(\text{Ca}) = +590\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$; $\text{IE}_2(\text{Ca}) = +1145\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$; $\Delta_{\text{atom}} H^\circ(\text{O}) = +249\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$; $\Delta_{\text{eg}} H_1(\text{O}) = -141\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$; lattice formation enthalpy $U_L(\text{CaO}) = -3414\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn:
By the Born–Haber cycle:
$\Delta_f H^\circ = \Delta_{\text{sub}} H^\circ + \text{IE}_1 + \text{IE}_2 + \Delta_{\text{atom}} H^\circ(\text{O}) + \Delta_{\text{eg}} H_1 + \Delta_{\text{eg}} H_2 + U_L$.
$-635 = 178 + 590 + 1145 + 249 - 141 + \Delta_{\text{eg}} H_2 - 3414 = -1393 + \Delta_{\text{eg}} H_2$.
Therefore, $\Delta_{\text{eg}} H_2 = 1393 - 635 = +758\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: If $y(x)$ satisfies the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2y = 4$ with $y(0) = 1$, then the value of $y\!\left(\dfrac{\ln 2}{2}\right)$ is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Rewriting as $\frac{dy}{2y + 4} = dx$ and integrating gives $\frac{1}{2}\ln|2y + 4| = x + C \implies y + 2 = A e^{2x}$. Using $y(0) = 1$ gives $A = 3$, so $y(x) = 3e^{2x} - 2$. At $x = \frac{\ln 2}{2}$, $e^{2x} = 2$, so $y = 3(2) - 2 = 4$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Mononitration of $13.5\text{ g}$ of acetanilide ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_9\text{NO}$) with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $0\text{--}5\,^\circ\text{C}$ yields *para*-nitroacetanilide ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_8\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$) in $75\%$ isolated yield. The mass of *para*-nitroacetanilide isolated is _______ $\text{g}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{N} = 14$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn:
Moles of acetanilide ($\text{MW} = 135\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) $= 13.5 / 135 = 0.100\text{ mol}$.
Molar mass of *para*-nitroacetanilide ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_8\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$) $= 8(12) + 8(1) + 2(14) + 3(16) = 180\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
Mass isolated at $75\%$ yield $= 0.100 \times 180 \times 0.75 = \mathbf{13.5}\text{ g}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The gyromagnetic ratio of the $^{13}\text{C}$ nucleus is $\gamma = 6.728 \times 10^7\text{ rad T}^{-1}\text{ s}^{-1}$. The Larmor resonance frequency of $^{13}\text{C}$ in a $9.40\text{ T}$ magnetic field is _______ $\text{MHz}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn: The Larmor frequency is $\nu = \frac{\gamma B_0}{2\pi} = \frac{6.728 \times 10^7 \times 9.40}{2\pi} = 1.0065 \times 10^8\text{ Hz} \approx 100.7\text{ MHz}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For *trans*-1-ethyl-4-methylcyclohexane, the conformational free energy difference between the diaxial and diequatorial chair conformers at $298\text{ K}$ is $\Delta G^\circ(aa \to ee) = -14.8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. Using $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, the equilibrium constant $K = [ee]/[aa]$ at $298\text{ K}$ is _______. *(round off to the nearest integer)*
questions.explanationEn: $K = \exp\left(-\frac{\Delta G^\circ}{RT}\right) = \exp\left(\frac{14800}{8.314 \times 298}\right) = \exp(5.9736) = 392.9 \approx 393$.

questions.questionTextEn: To $1.0\text{ L}$ of an aqueous buffer containing $0.20\text{ M}$ $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ ($\text{p}K_a = 4.76$) and $0.20\text{ M}$ $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$, $0.040\text{ mol}$ of gaseous $\text{HCl}$ is added with negligible volume change. The $\text{pH}$ of the resulting solution is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: The added $\text{HCl}$ reacts quantitatively with $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$: $[\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-] = 0.20 - 0.040 = 0.16\text{ M}$ and $[\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}] = 0.20 + 0.040 = 0.24\text{ M}$. By Henderson–Hasselbalch, $\text{pH} = 4.76 + \log_{10}\left(\frac{0.16}{0.24}\right) = 4.76 - 0.176 = 4.58$.
